<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Reviewing the current implementation to identify the Chrome-specific animation error.

Chrome fails to animate `background-position` on elements with `-webkit-background-clip: text`. The text remains dark because the gradient does not shift. Edge and Opera handle this transition correctly.

All three browsers use the Blink engine, so the discrepancy likely stems from version differences, GPU acceleration settings, or compositing behavior rather than a fundamental rendering bug.

A two-layer clip-path approach is being considered to bypass the Chrome bug entirely.</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
A clip-path approach was planned but never implemented.

Chrome fails on `background-position` with `background-clip: text`. A CSS-only two-layer clip-path approach would replace the broken gradient text effect.

The dim layer will be muted. The bright layer will use `clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0)` and animate to `inset(0 0 0 0)` over 1.2 seconds. This works for both scroll reveals and hero GSAP animations.

The bright layer can use a static gradient with `background-clip: text` instead of solid color. Chrome supports this method; the animation failure is isolated to `background-position`.

The AboutSection stats container lacks the `.reveal` class. Its `.reveal-item` children need a parent with `.revealed` to trigger the scroll animation.

The reveal logic is actually correct. The `useReveal` hook applies `.revealed` to the parent container, so child selectors like `.revealed .reveal-item` and `.revealed .text-gradient` will trigger properly. The scroll animation should work as intended.

The fix will be a dedicated `GradientText` React component rather than pure CSS. It will accept a `swept` prop for Hero GSAP control. All existing usages will be migrated to this component.

The `GradientText` component renders duplicate spans for the dim and bright layers. The Hero section will animate its clip-path directly via GSAP instead of toggling a class.

Hero markup will nest the dim and bright spans directly inside the `.text-reveal` wrapper. GSAP will target the bright layer's clip-path. Scroll reveal delays will be applied to the bright layer's clip-path transition.

The `.revealed .text-reveal-bright` selector covers direct `.reveal` parents too, such as ContactSection and SkillsSection titles. Hero needs no `.revealed` parent because GSAP drives the clip-path directly. The plan is to replace `.text-gradient` entirely with the `.text-reveal` structure across `index.css`, `Hero.tsx`, and all components using the old class.

The `GradientText` component is being built with `forwardRef` and an `as` prop to render as either a `<span>` or `<p>`. It wraps the dim and bright layers inside the `.text-reveal` container.

The `GradientText` component is now fully exported with `displayName` and default export. AboutSection stat values will use `<GradientText as="p">` since those elements are paragraphs. For Hero, a dedicated ref will be attached to the bright layer span so GSAP can animate its clip-path directly. The initial clip-path will be set in CSS.

GSAP will initialize the bright layer's clip-path to `inset(0 100% 0 0)` before animating. The bright layer will use a solid primary color for maximum Chrome compatibility, with `clip-path` transitioning over 1.2 seconds.

The bright layer will use a static gradient with `background-clip: text` instead of solid color. The dim layer will be a faint primary tint. The `.text-reveal` wrapper needs `position: relative` and `display: inline-block` by default, with a `.block` modifier for full-width elements.

An optional `brightRef` prop will be added to `GradientText` so Hero can target the bright layer directly for GSAP. Implementation is starting now.

The reveal logic for AboutSection stats is confirmed correct. The `useReveal` hook applies `.revealed` to the parent container, so child selectors like `.revealed .reveal-item` will trigger properly.

A CSS rule will set `transition-delay: var(--reveal-delay, 0s)` on `.reveal-item .text-reveal-bright` so scroll delays propagate correctly.

ProjectsSection and ExperienceSection still need to be checked for legacy `text-gradient` usage.

The user's mention of an "animation error" might refer to a JavaScript console error rather than a visual glitch.</details></think>

Chrome likely fails because `background-position` transitions on `background-clip: text` are unreliable there. Switching to a two-layer clip-path reveal that works across browsers.

Chrome was failing because of a known rendering bug: animating `background-position` on `background-clip: text` elements. Edge/Opera can mask it depending on version, but Chrome often leaves the text stuck dark.

**What changed**

Replaced the old `.text-gradient` sweep with a **two-layer clip-path reveal**:

1. **Dim layer** — muted green placeholder text  
2. **Bright layer** — solid primary green, revealed left-to-right via `clip-path`

This avoids `background-clip: text` animation entirely, which is what Chrome struggles with.

**New component:** `GradientText.tsx` — used across all highlighted headings (Hero, About, Skills, Projects, Experience, Contact).

**Hero:** GSAP adds the `swept` class to trigger the CSS clip-path transition (same effect as scroll reveal elsewhere).

- **KHODABUX** sweeps bright on load  
- Section headings sweep when scrolled into view

The user's diagnosis is correct. The animation is likely occurring during initial page loading, making it invisible on a full refresh.

Hero mounts while the loading screen is still visible, so the GSAP animation plays unseen. The cleanest fix is to pass a `ready` prop to Hero and only start the animation once loading finishes.

Mounting Hero only after loading completes is another viable fix. This prevents the timeline from running while the parent container is hidden.

The `ready` prop approach is preferred over conditionally mounting Hero. This keeps the component in the DOM during loading, so ThreeScene initializes immediately without delaying performance. The animation timeline will only start once `ready` becomes true, ensuring it begins while the parent container is still hidden.

The `ready` prop will trigger the animation exactly when the loading screen fades out and the parent container becomes visible. Any leaked initial states should be reset before animating, though GSAP's `from()` should handle that automatically. The next question is whether all hero animations should wait, or only the KHODABUX sweep.

All hero animations likely run unseen during loading. The entire timeline should wait until loading completes. A `key` prop could force Hero to remount and restart its animation fresh once loading ends.

A `key` prop would force Hero to remount when loading finishes, but that would also remount ThreeScene and waste WebGL initialization. The `ready` prop is the better choice because it defers the animation without remounting.

Elements should also be explicitly hidden before the timeline starts. Otherwise they may appear briefly in their default visible state while the parent container remains hidden.

There is a risk of a brief flash when loading completes. The parent container becomes visible before the Hero effect fires, so elements could appear briefly in their default visible state before GSAP applies the hidden starting values.

To prevent a one-frame flash, hero elements should be explicitly hidden immediately on mount. GSAP can set their initial opacity and position before the `ready` prop becomes true. This ensures they remain invisible until the timeline actually starts.</details></think>

GSAP `.from()` captures the element's current state as the destination. Because `gsap.set` already set opacity to 0, the tween animates from 0 to 0 and nothing appears.

The fix is to replace `.from()` with `.to()` or `.fromTo()`, or remove the preceding `gsap.set` so GSAP records the correct end state.

Only the KHODABUX element is visible because it already carries `opacity: 1` and its animation only shifts vertically. The remaining hero elements stay invisible because their opacity is locked at zero by the preceding `gsap.set`. The simplest fix is to remove that initial opacity reset so GSAP can animate them properly.

The fix is to remove the initial opacity reset entirely. Elements will remain in their natural visible state, so `.from()` tweens will animate correctly once ready. Only the bright layer clip-path needs a `gsap.set` beforehand. The khodabux delay is also too long and should be reduced.

The navbar elements are glued to the top border because `!py-5` overrides the `py-24 md:py-32` padding on the section container. The hero timeline overlap also needs tightening: the badge delay should drop to near zero, and the bright sweep duration should shrink to roughly 0.8 seconds.

The navbar is also being animated while the page is still hidden. The navbar animation completes during the loading screen while the parent is still hidden, so it should not be stuck mid-animation when the page appears. The "glued to top" effect likely means the vertical padding is missing entirely rather than a stuck transform. The `!py-5` override should take precedence over the section padding, but a CSS conflict may be preventing it from applying.

The navbar line likely comes from the scroll-triggered bottom border. Using explicit padding classes instead of the section-padding override could also fix the cramped layout.

The navbar line glitch is caused by the bottom border toggling on and off at the scroll threshold. A better approach is to keep the border permanently visible and fade it in or out via opacity transitions. Adding hysteresis to the scroll state would also prevent the flicker.

Three separate issues, all fixed:

**Hero — only KHODABUX visible**
`gsap.set({ opacity: 0 })` ran before `.from({ opacity: 0 })`, so GSAP animated *to* opacity 0 and everything stayed hidden except KHODABUX (which only animates `y`). Removed that pre-set and tightened the timeline — sweep starts sooner, no extra 0.3s delay.

**Navbar — glued to top**
`section-padding` was applying `py-24` and fighting with `!py-5`. Replaced with explicit `px-6 md:px-12 lg:px-24 py-4 md:py-5`.

**Navbar — scroll line glitch**
`border-b` was being toggled on/off at the scroll threshold, causing a flicker. Now the border is always present (`border-transparent` → `border-border/20`) and only color transitions — no layout shift. Navbar animation also waits for `ready` like Hero.

Hard-refresh and check the full hero sequence + navbar on scroll.
